author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if getting more sleep could boost your grades and transform your life? The Eight Hour Sleep Challenge proves that prioritizing rest, even during life’s most stressful moments, enhances focus, productivity, and overall well-being. 

Dr. Scullin completed his doctorate in the Behavior, Brain, and Cognition program at Washington University in St. Louis and then a post-doctoral fellowship in the Neurology and Sleep Medicine program at Emory University School of Medicine. He is involved in service committees for the Sleep Research Society, he is a columnist for Teaching Current Directions in Psychological Science at APS, and he co-founded the APA journal Translational Issues in Psychological Science. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: I give students extra credit for sleeping—here’s why | Michael Scullin | TEDxBaylor University

description:
In a world teaching us to close off, protect ourselves and harden, what if the real power of leadership lies in staying open? From ancient Arab civilizations to modern-day acts of radical hospitality across the UAE, Marilyn Zakhour explores why leading with an open heart builds stronger communities, greater trust and lasting human connection. This is a powerful reflection on leadership Marilyn Zakhour is the founder and CEO of Cosmic Centaurs, an organizational and leadership development firm. Marilyn is former CMO of EMAAR and CEO of Dubai Opera. She blends the agility of startups and the excellence of multinationals in every mission.

She is a two-time Harvard Business Review author, a university lecturer, and the host of two podcasts where she examines the evolving nature of leadership and the workplace. Through her writing, research, and open-source frameworks, Marilyn is on a mission to redefine what great leadership looks like and where the world looks for it. This talk was give
title: What The Arab World Can Teach Us About Leadership | Marilyn Zakhour | TEDxAl Wasl Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In the wake of a life-changing event, time seems to stop. But in this stillness, we find that
nothing is ever truly motionless. The planet keeps spinning, moving with oscillations we barely
notice. We move forward by finding these small steps, sustaining motion even when it looks
different. Understanding that everything moves, even in our most frozen moments, becomes the
key to building momentum one steady pulse at a time. Jennifer Gearin is a sophomore at the University of Connecticut pursuing a B.S. in Physics with minors in Astrophysics and Linguistics.
As well as being drawn to theoretical astrophysics and mathematics, she also studies the ways we understand, interpret, and communicate scientific knowledge. With the Life Purpose Lab, she has researched how meaning and motivation influence human behavior.
Beyond academics, she is a competitive and professional figure skater who loves her dog, family, and friends more than anything, and will often be found playing the crossword. Thi
title: Motion in Stillness | Jennifer Gearin | TEDxUConn

author: TEDx Talks
description: Relationships are some of the most fundamental aspects of humans' lives. They are associated with greater longevity, lower morbidity, and well-being. Not having relationships is associated with poorer physical and mental health. Recently loneliness was named an epidemic in the United States. In this talk, I will discuss the value of relationships, including why they matter and everyday activities that can improve or harm them to connect with the theme of Onward and Upward. I will also discuss different types of relationships, including brand relationships. Marketing professor Danielle Brick specializes in research on consumer relationships, including brand and interpersonal relationships. She is particularly interested in the impact of shared decisions and experiences, power, and resources within relationships on consumer well-being. Her research has been published in top academic journals, such as the Journal of Consumer Research, Journal of Consumer Psychology, and Journal of the As
title: The surprising effects of brand preferences on relationships | Dr. Danielle Brick | TEDxUConn

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world where money shapes opportunity, security, and freedom, financial literacy remains inaccessible to far too many people, even while being in front of our very own eyes. In this talk, Andrea Perez-Meneses explores how gaps in financial knowledge are not accidental, but systemic, and how reclaiming that knowledge can be a powerful tool for individual and generational transformation. Drawing from her work in financial education, leadership, and advocacy, she challenges the idea that wealth is reserved for the few and reframes from money as a skill that can be learned, taught, and shared. This talk is a call to rethink our relationship with money, build confidence around financial decision-making, and take intentional steps toward long-term empowerment, for ourselves and for those who come after us. Andrea Perez-Meneses is an economics student and campus leader at the University of Connecticut with a strong focus on financial literacy and long-term empowerment. Her work centers o
title: The Undervalued Problem | Andrea Perez-Meneses | TEDxUConn

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The humanities are often labeled as some of the most “useless” degrees, a perception that has grown as students have been encouraged to abandon them for higher-paying STEM fields. But these misconceptions have pushed us away from the very skills society depends on most. Literature, storytelling, and the arts are not luxuries, but tools for survival. As education prioritizes efficiency over empathy and utility over meaning, we risk losing these essential tools. What happens when a society can read, but can’t understand? 
In an era of rising illiteracy and rapidly spreading misinformation, the ability to critically analyze language is essential across every discipline in everyday life. More than half of American adults struggle to read above a sixth-grade level, yet the ability to identify meaning, credibility, and bias is essential for a functioning democracy. These are the same skills cultivated by philosophy, history, and the visual arts. STEM does not exist without the humanities; i
title: Rethinking Progress: How the Humanities Shape Our Future | Nyanna Pannu | TEDxUConn

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We live life through our own perspective, casting ourselves as the central character in our hero's journey while others play supporting roles or obstacles. Yet in their narrative, we may be the obstacle, or even the villain. This talk explores the concept of multi-perspectivity, a storytelling technique that reveals how meaning shifts depending on narrative point of view. It's as if we're living in a Severance-themed world, with both an "outie" story we're living, full of experiences and interactions, and an "innie" story of thoughts and interpretations influencing our behaviors.

By recognizing that our colleague, neighbor, or even the driver who cut us off is living a different inner story, we can move beyond an “us vs. them" mentality, expanding our perspectives and elevating our interactions, the theme of this year's "Onwards and Upwards" TEDx event.  Valerie Gordon believes in the power of story. A television producer with credits at CBS News, ESPN, HBO Sports, and other outlets,
title: Heroes vs. Villains: Whose Story is it? | Valerie Gordon | TEDxUConn | Valerie Gordon | TEDxUConn

description: The future belongs to organizations that multiply leadership across people, not positions. Debbie Nicol explores how Executive Presence can transform teams from dependent followers into empowered contributors who carry the mission forward together. Debbie Nicol is an Australian-born leadership strategist and founder of UAE-based business en motion. For over three decades, she has helped strengthen leadership, culture and change capability, guiding senior leaders and organizations through complex transformation, often in environments defined by diversity, rapid growth and continual change. A long-term resident of the UAE, Debbie is a trusted advisor recognized for bridging human dynamics with systemic design. Describing herself as a 'body of curiosity’, Debbie continually stretches her own growth through sea and mountain-based outdoor pursuits and adventures. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more
title: Why Leadership Dependency is Disrupting Organizations | Debbie Nicol | TEDxAl Wasl Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: "The Silicon Valley innovation model needs a makeover. For the past few decades, as the digital world has consumed modern society, we've been increasingly faced with products and services that generate clicks, collect data, and hold our attention hostage for virtually nothing in return. The modern tech landscape prioritizes profits over users, and the problem has only exacerbated as with the entrance of venture capital firms into the sector. To address this backwards institutional culture, we must look critically at our most influential technological developments and incorporate ethical design into our engineering practices." Nathan Miller is a 2024 graduate of UConn’s School of Business and CLAS. He designed his own major focusing on human-computer interaction, ethical technology design, and digital well-being. His writing focuses on how people engage with technology, looking at social media, the tech market, and consumer behavior. After graduating, he worked on social impact campaig
title: Flying cars, they said | Nathan Miller | TEDxUConn

description:
What happens when the box the world puts you in becomes too small for who you are meant to be?
​For a long time, Jean lived inside a "frame" built by self-doubt, shrinking just to blend in. We convince ourselves that staying hidden is safe, but true growth requires a deliberate choice to look at the narrative you’ve been handed and completely rewrite it.
​In this talk, Jean shares his journey from a shy kid hiding in the background to standing confidently in his own light. This is a rallying cry for anyone tired of playing a side character or waiting for permission to be great. Stop shrinking for the comfort of others. Break the frame, it’s time to claim your space Grade 12 student This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Num poema falado, o Poeta da Cidade confronta a cultura da aspiração sem limite. Quem somos quando nos tornamos produto dos sonhos de terceiros, peças de uma fábrica que vende ambição e a devolve com defeito? Entre a queda de Ícaro, que voa até o sol lhe queimar as penas, e a tentação de escolher dormir só para sonhar mais, esta performance pergunta o que perdemos quando preferimos a fantasia à realidade.
 Poeta, dizedor e performer, Pedro Freitas tem 26 anos e é hoje uma das vozes mais reconhecidas da poesia portuguesa contemporânea.

Iniciou o seu percurso artístico no concurso Dá Voz à Letra, da Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian, afirmando-se desde então como um dos dizedores de poesia mais escutados em Portugal. 

Publicou de forma independente o seu primeiro livro, Ela, Metafisicamente d’outro Mundo, que se tornou o livro de poesia portuguesa mais vendido desse ano e do ano seguinte. Lançou Vim Sem Tempo, distinguido com o Prémio Melhor Livro do Ano pela Bertrand.

title: Sonhos | Poeta da Cidade  | TEDxLisboa

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Assister à la descente aux enfers de son conjoint et se sentir impuissante face à cette situation, c’est le témoignage que nous livre Carito. Seule avec deux enfants en bas âge, elle nous raconte comment elle a accepté le chaos pour mieux le défier et le battre à force de patience et de remise en question des injonctions de perfection qui nous sont faites. "Vivre l’alcoolisme par procuration.
Mais vivre aussi sa vie d’épouse, de femme et de mère de deux adolescentes.
Voici ce que Carito nous invite à découvrir : l’alcoolisme, une maladie secrète qui impacte tout un univers. Un voyage familial dans les méandres d’une souffrance partagée lorsque c’est l’être aimé qui est atteint par cette maladie.
" This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Injonctions, alcoolisme et résilience | Carito VARGAS-TORRES | TEDxRennes

description:
La technologie ne nous sauvera pas. Pour faire face aux défis d'une monde contraint, la low tech, amie de la high tech s'impose par sa frugalité. A l'avenir tout sera question de choix et d’équilibre entre les deux, dans le respect des limites planétaires. Découvrez votre vie dans un monde low-tech, loin des clichés et des aprioris. Auteur de dix livres dont deux romans, Alan est une figure majeure de la low-tech.
Fondateur de Goodwill-management, cabinet de conseil en performance économique responsable, il est également président de l’agence qui délivre le label LUCIE 26 000, (premier label français de responsabilité sociétale des entreprises aligné sur l’ISO 26000 -1400 membres). Il est enfin président de Kerlotec, écosystème d’entreprises low-tech en Bretagne et c’est sur ce sujet qu’il intervient au TEDxRennes 2025. Vous connaissez la high tech mais la low tech ne vous dit rien ? Et pourtant, dans un monde contraint, c’est quasi une évidence. This talk was given at a TEDx event us
title: Low tech : et si le bonheur était une soustraction | Alan FUSTEC | TEDxRennes

author: TEDx Talks
description: Saviez-vous que la nature possède son propre langage, totalement invisible à nos yeux ? Loin d’être toxique ou purement synthétique, la chimie est au cœur de toutes les interactions du vivant.  Dans ce talk TEDxRennes, Soizic Prado, professeure et chimiste des produits naturels au Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle, nous invite à tendre l'oreille — ou plutôt le nez — vers ces messages secrets. Spécialiste de l'écologie chimique et coordinatrice de projets d’envergure nationale et européenne, elle décrypte comment les plantes, les micro-organismes et les animaux utilisent les molécules pour s'entraider, se défendre ou séduire.  Des élans de solidarité des tomates aux ruses des insectes, elle dévoile un équilibre fascinant mais aujourd'hui grandement menacé par la crise climatique. Un voyage passionnant qui prouve qu'en comprenant ce langage microscopique, la science peut s'en inspirer pour créer la médecine et les solutions durables de demain. "Soizic Prado est professeure, chimiste
title: Le langage chimique invisible de la nature | Soizic PRADO | TEDxRennes

author: TEDx Talks
description: Anesthesiologist Dr. Nina Apra explores the concept of "Syntopia," a state of inner harmony where the body, mind, heart, and soul are fully aligned. She argues that while modern society is obsessed with optimizing external metrics like productivity and digital presence, it often neglects the wisdom of the body and the necessity of human touch. Drawing from her experiences in critical care, she highlights how clinical machines—while precise—cannot replace the neurobiological benefits of direct human connection. Dr. Apra encourages prioritizing honesty and self-awareness over mere efficiency, urging people to listen to their bodies before their calendars. Ultimately, she defines Syntopia as the moment when technology serves humanity and one's heartbeat learns to communicate with their algorithms Dr. Nina Apra is a qualified Anesthesiologist and currently serves as the Chief Medical Officer at a regional hospital under South Eastern Coalfields Limited (Coal India Ltd.), based in Chhattis
title: SYNTOPIA BEGINS WITHIN : WHEN HEARTBEAT TALKS TO  AN ALGORITHM | Nina Apra | TEDxMSU Baroda

What Wildlife Taught Me About Being Human 

In this talk, wildlife veterinarian Dr. Nikita Mehta shares how working with injured and rescued wild animals unexpectedly changed the way she understands uncertainty, patience, and human behaviour. Through real clinical cases and rescue situations, she reflects on the tendency to seek quick answers - and what wildlife taught her instead. Nikita, wildlife veterinarian with extensive hands-on experience at a
24-hour wildlife transit treatment centre, managing rescues, emergency care, rehabilitation, and successful release of urban, semi-urban, and rural wildlife. Skilled in chemical immobilization and frontline management of human-wildlife conflict cases, including leopard attacks, monkey conflicts, and accident trauma. Passionate about orphan care, reptile medicine, and solving human-animal conflict challenges with a focus on both animal welfare and community support. Deeply committed to the One Health approach, with a strong interest in zoo
title: Leading with Empathy | Nikita Metha | TEDxSIS Pune Youth

In this talk, Jake explores the popular phrase “locking in” as more than just a trend. He connects it to the discipline, focus, and resilience needed to face uncertainty and overcome challenges. 

Drawing from his experience as a Member of Parliament, Jake reflects on how young people can stay grounded when life feels unpredictable, commit to what matters, and keep moving forward even when the path is unclear. The talk would encourage youth to see “locking in” not as pressure to be perfect, but as a mindset for purpose, growth, and perseverance.
